postgresql.connections.ref: https://docs.datadoghq.com/opentelemetry/guide/metrics_mapping/ (postgresql.connections <-> postgresql.backends); labels from docs/DASH0_INVENTORY.md. Semantic note: backends counts all backend types; Datadog connections counts numbackends. Grain dedups resource-hash churn (docs/DASH0_INVENTORY.md#caveats). Assumption (not reviewed): grain labels include postgresql_database_name because Datadog postgresql.connections is per database; with service_instance_id alone, avg:postgresql.connections{*} took the max over databases instead of averaging them

postgresql.percent_usage_connections.expression: sum by (service_instance_id) (max by (service_instance_id, postgresql_database_name) ({otel_metric_name="postgresql.backends", otel_metric_type="sum"$filters})) / on (service_instance_id) max by (service_instance_id) ({otel_metric_name="postgresql.connection.max", otel_metric_type="gauge"$filters})
postgresql.percent_usage_connections.ref: Derived: Datadog postgresql.percent_usage_connections = connections / max_connections (no 1:1 OTel metric). Dedup per docs/DASH0_INVENTORY.md#caveats. postgresql.connection.max carries service_instance_id (Dash0 check 2026-11-07: count by (otel_metric_name, cpu_mode, system_network_direction, service_instance_id, host_name) (last_over_time({otel_metric_name=~...}[1h])) on dataset default)

postgresql.rows_deleted.ref: https://docs.datadoghq.com/opentelemetry/guide/metrics_mapping/ (postgresql.rows_deleted <-> postgresql.tup_deleted); Datadog reports a per-second rate of a cumulative counter; target type checked in Dash0 (Dash0 check 2026-11-07: count by (otel_metric_name, cpu_mode, system_network_direction, service_instance_id, host_name) (last_over_time({otel_metric_name=~...}[1h])) on dataset default); Grain (assumption, not reviewed): max by (service_instance_id, postgresql_database_name) collapses resource-hash duplicates (docs/DASH0_INVENTORY.md#caveats, item 2) while keeping one series per database, so sums and averages over databases keep their meaning; a grain on service_instance_id alone would turn a sum over databases into a max.

system.net.bytes_rcvd.ref: https://docs.datadoghq.com/opentelemetry/guide/metrics_mapping/ (system.net.bytes_rcvd <-> system.network.io, direction receive); label values checked in Dash0 (Dash0 check 2026-11-07: count by (otel_metric_name, cpu_mode, system_network_direction, service_instance_id, host_name) (last_over_time({otel_metric_name=~...}[1h])) on dataset default); Loopback is kept: Datadog's network check excludes no interface by default (integrations-core@a9b9e42 network/datadog_checks/network/network.py: excluded_interfaces defaults to []; spec.yaml lists lo/lo0 only as an example; the agent's shipped network.d/conf.yaml.default sets no exclusion), and the OTel hostmetrics network scraper also includes every interface unless configured. No grain (assumption, not reviewed): a max by (service_instance_id) would turn the sum over interfaces and hosts into a max, and a dedup on (host_name, network_interface_name) relies on labels not yet verified on system.network.io; resource-hash duplicates were only observed on Postgres series.
